```tsx
"use client";

import {
  EllipsisVerticalIcon,
  CopyIcon,
  ClipboardPasteIcon,
  TrashIcon,
} from "lucide-react";
import { Button } from "../ui/button";
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from "../ui/dropdown-menu";

/**
 * Props for {@link BlockActionsMenu}.
 */
export interface BlockActionsMenuProps {
  index: number;
  count: number;
  readOnly: boolean;
  canAdd: boolean;
  blockLabel: string;
  onDuplicate: () => void;
  onInsertAbove: () => void;
  onInsertBelow: () => void;
  onMoveUp: () => void;
  onMoveDown: () => void;
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Copies this single block to the block clipboard. Never gated on `readOnly` — copying does not mutate the field. */
  onCopy: () => void;
  /** Pastes the current block clipboard contents above this block. */
  onPasteAbove: () => void;
  /** Pastes the current block clipboard contents below this block. */
  onPasteBelow: () => void;
  /** Whether the clipboard has at least one block this field accepts and pasting it would not exceed `max`. */
  canPaste: boolean;
}

/**
 * Per-block actions menu — duplicate, copy, paste above/below, insert
 * above/below, move up/down, delete.
 *
 * @param props - See {@link BlockActionsMenuProps}.
 * @returns A `DropdownMenu` trigger button and its menu content.
 */
export function BlockActionsMenu(props: BlockActionsMenuProps) {
  const isFirst = props.index === 0;
  const isLast = props.index === props.count - 1;

  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger
        render={
          <Button
            type="button"
            variant="ghost"
            size="icon-xs"
            className="shrink-0 text-muted-foreground"
            aria-label={`${props.blockLabel} actions`}
          >
            <EllipsisVerticalIcon className="size-3.5" />
          </Button>
        }
      />
      <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || !props.canAdd}
          onClick={props.onDuplicate}
        >
          Duplicate
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={props.onCopy}>
          <CopyIcon /> Copy
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || !props.canPaste}
          onClick={props.onPasteAbove}
        >
          <ClipboardPasteIcon /> Paste above
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || !props.canPaste}
          onClick={props.onPasteBelow}
        >
          <ClipboardPasteIcon /> Paste below
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || !props.canAdd}
          onClick={props.onInsertAbove}
        >
          Insert above
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || !props.canAdd}
          onClick={props.onInsertBelow}
        >
          Insert below
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || isFirst}
          onClick={props.onMoveUp}
        >
          Move up
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem
          disabled={props.readOnly || isLast}
          onClick={props.onMoveDown}
        >
          Move down
        </DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuSeparator />
        <DropdownMenuItem
          variant="destructive"
          disabled={props.readOnly}
          onClick={props.onRemove}
        >
          <TrashIcon /> Remove
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  );
}
```

**2. Paste resolution + toast summary helpers** — new module-level functions, anchored after `computeDefaultOpenBlocks`.

```ts
/**
 * Matches clipboard blocks against the target field's block definitions by
 * `blockType`. Unknown `blockType`s are skipped; known blocks are coerced to
 * the target definition (unknown keys dropped, missing keys defaulted) and
 * get fresh ids (nested blocks too) so pasting never collides with an
 * existing item's id — including re-pasting into the field it was copied
 * from.
 *
 * @param props - The clipboard's blocks and the target field's block
 *   definitions keyed by `blockType`.
 * @returns The accepted, paste-ready blocks plus counts for the paste's
 *   toast summary.
 */
function resolvePasteCandidates(props: {
  blocks: GenericBlock[];
  blockDefMap: Map<string, BlockConfig>;
}): { accepted: GenericBlock[]; skipped: number; droppedKeys: number } {
  let skipped = 0;
  let droppedKeys = 0;
  const accepted: GenericBlock[] = [];
  for (const block of props.blocks) {
    const blockDef = props.blockDefMap.get(block.blockType as string);
    if (!blockDef) {
      skipped += 1;
      continue;
    }
    const coerced = coerceBlockToDefinition({ block, blockDef });
    droppedKeys += coerced.droppedKeys.length;
    accepted.push(cloneBlockWithFreshIds({ block: coerced.block, blockDef }));
  }
  return { accepted, skipped, droppedKeys };
}

/**
 * Summarizes a paste outcome as a single toast — accepted count, plus how
 * many clipboard blocks were skipped (unsupported `blockType`) and how many
 * fields were dropped off the accepted blocks (not part of the target
 * block's definition).
 *
 * @param props - The paste outcome to summarize.
 */
function toastPasteOutcome(props: {
  acceptedCount: number;
  skipped: number;
  droppedKeys: number;
}): void {
  if (props.acceptedCount === 0) {
    toast.error("Nothing in the clipboard matches this field's block types.");
    return;
  }
  const parts = [
    `Pasted ${props.acceptedCount} block${props.acceptedCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}.`,
  ];
  if (props.skipped > 0) {
    parts.push(
      `Skipped ${props.skipped} unsupported block${props.skipped === 1 ? "" : "s"}.`,
    );
  }
  if (props.droppedKeys > 0) {
    parts.push(
      `Dropped ${props.droppedKeys} field${props.droppedKeys === 1 ? "" : "s"} not in this block's definition.`,
    );
  }
  toast(parts.join(" "));
}
```

**3. Clipboard state, paste candidates and gating** — anchored after `atMax`/`maxValue` (step 15).

```ts
const { clipboard, copyBlocks } = useBlockClipboard();
const [replaceAllOpen, setReplaceAllOpen] = useState(false);
const pasteCandidates = resolvePasteCandidates({
  blocks: clipboard?.blocks ?? [],
  blockDefMap,
});
const pasteWouldExceedMax =
  maxValue !== undefined &&
  items.length + pasteCandidates.accepted.length > maxValue;
const replaceWouldExceedMax =
  maxValue !== undefined && pasteCandidates.accepted.length > maxValue;
const canPaste =
  !effectiveReadOnly &&
  pasteCandidates.accepted.length > 0 &&
  !pasteWouldExceedMax;
const canReplaceAll =
  !effectiveReadOnly &&
  pasteCandidates.accepted.length > 0 &&
  !replaceWouldExceedMax;
```

**4. Copy/paste handlers** — anchored after `updateBlockName`.

```ts
function handleCopyAll() {
  copyBlocks({ blocks: items });
  toast(`Copied ${items.length} block${items.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}.`);
}

function handleCopyBlock(block: GenericBlock) {
  copyBlocks({ blocks: [block] });
  toast(
    `Copied "${(block.blockName as string) || (block.blockType as string)}".`,
  );
}

function handlePasteAppend() {
  if (!canPaste) return;
  field.handleChange([...items, ...pasteCandidates.accepted]);
  toastPasteOutcome({
    acceptedCount: pasteCandidates.accepted.length,
    skipped: pasteCandidates.skipped,
    droppedKeys: pasteCandidates.droppedKeys,
  });
}

function handlePasteAt(index: number, position: "above" | "below") {
  if (!canPaste) return;
  const insertIndex = position === "above" ? index : index + 1;
  const updated = [...items];
  updated.splice(insertIndex, 0, ...pasteCandidates.accepted);
  field.handleChange(updated);
  toastPasteOutcome({
    acceptedCount: pasteCandidates.accepted.length,
    skipped: pasteCandidates.skipped,
    droppedKeys: pasteCandidates.droppedKeys,
  });
}

function handleReplaceAll() {
  if (!canReplaceAll) return;
  field.handleChange(pasteCandidates.accepted);
  setReplaceAllOpen(false);
  toastPasteOutcome({
    acceptedCount: pasteCandidates.accepted.length,
    skipped: pasteCandidates.skipped,
    droppedKeys: pasteCandidates.droppedKeys,
  });
}
```

#### packages/react/src/components/form/BlockActionsMenu.tsx (slot wiring)

Builds on step 15's `SlotOutlet`-driven menu (`SLOT_IDS.blocks.itemActions`) — the three new

Why: closes the remaining "half-built" inputs and ignored `cellAlignment`, and the
state sweep surfaces defects the per-type contract tests never caught because they
individually pass (`hasInertSignal` accepts ANY inert signal, so a passive
`aria-readonly` counted the same as a real `disabled`) while the visible behavior
disagrees across types.

**This step builds on Steps 1, 2, 3, 6 and 10 as landed, not on today's repo.** In
particular: `text`/`number`/`email`/`url` all carry Step 1's `FieldLimit` tuples
(`field.min`/`field.max` are `readonly [value, error] | undefined`, never the old
`{ value, error }` object); `email()` exists (Step 2) with the same `FieldLimit`
min/max semantics as `text`; `textarea()` exists (Step 3) and its counter markup
(`components/fields/textarea/Input.tsx`) is what `text`'s counter below reuses
verbatim — same `<p className="self-end text-[0.8rem] text-muted-foreground
tabular-nums">{value.length}/{fieldDef.max[0]}</p>`; `FieldAdminConfigInput`/
`FieldAdminConfig` (`baseTypes.ts`) carry Step 6's `width: string` (default
`"100%"`) — every field's `admin` defaults object below already includes
`width: "100%"`, not the pre-Step-6 `width: "full"`; there is no `layout`
property in this model; and `text`/`email`/`number`/`url` each render **two**
branches from Step 10's `admin.mask` support — a masked, uncontrolled `<Input
ref={maskRef} defaultValue={…} onInput={…}>` and an unmasked, controlled `<Input
value={…} onChange={…}>` — so every fix below (both-source `disabled`,
`aria-invalid`) is applied to **both** branches, and `step`/`min`/`max` HTML
attributes are applied **only** to number's unmasked `type="number"` branch (a
masked number renders `type="text"`, where those attributes are inert). `select`
is untouched by Steps 1/2/3/10 (not maskable, no `min`/`max`) — its edits below are
unaffected by any of this and match what was already written against the
pre-mask repo.

**Audit findings (file:line as read against the Step-10-landed tree; ordered by
severity):**

1. **`packages/react/src/components/fields/select/Input.tsx:75-77`** — real functional
   bug, not just visual. `fieldDef.admin.readOnly` only set `aria-readonly` on
   `MultiSelectTrigger`, a plain informational ARIA attribute `PopoverTrigger` (a
   button) never enforces — the popover still opened and selections still worked
   with `admin.readOnly: true` and the `readOnly` prop `false`. Only the `readOnly`
   _prop_ actually disabled the control (`disabled={readOnly}`). Fixed: both sources
   now drive `disabled`, matching every other field type's own OR-composition
   (already documented at `upload/Input.tsx:42-45`).
2. **No field `Input.tsx` ever sets `aria-invalid`** — `text`, `email`, `number`,
   `url`, `select`, `color` (`Input.tsx:186-197`), `checkbox` (`Input.tsx:45-54`).
   The base `Input`/`Checkbox`/`Button` primitives already ship
   `aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-3 aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20`
   (`ui/input.tsx:54`, `ui/checkbox.tsx:12`) — dead CSS, because nothing ever set the
   attribute. `FormError` shows the message; the control itself never visually
   agreed. Fixed for the seven single-control types this step owns via a new shared
   `isFieldShowingError` helper (`form/FormError.tsx`), using the exact same
   touched/submissionAttempts timing `FormError` already uses, so the ring and the
   message always appear together — wired onto **both** the masked and unmasked
   `<Input>` branches for `text`/`email`/`number`/`url` (Step 10).
3. **`packages/react/src/components/ui/multi-select.tsx:138-141`** — `MultiSelectTrigger`
   carried no `aria-invalid:*` variant at all (unlike `ui/input.tsx`/`ui/checkbox.tsx`/
   `ui/button.tsx`), so even after (2) nothing would have rendered. Fixed alongside (2).
4. **`packages/react/src/components/fields/text/Input.tsx:786,798`,
   `url/Input.tsx:1065,1077`, `email/Input.tsx:1204,1217`** (Step-10-landed line
   numbers, both the masked and unmasked `<Input>`) — `disabled={readOnly}` only;
   `fieldDef.admin.readOnly` was forwarded solely as the native HTML `readonly`
   attribute, which blocks editing but carries none of
   `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed` — a field marked
   `admin.readOnly: true` looked fully active. `number`'s own Step-10 output already
   uses `disabled={readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly}` on both branches (not part
   of this defect); `text`/`email`/`url` now match it.
5. **`packages/react/src/components/ui/data-table/DataTable.tsx:239-258`** — every
   `*FieldToColumnDef` factory sets `meta.align` from `fieldDef.admin.cellAlignment`
   (e.g. `text/columnDef.tsx:60-64`), and `TableHead`/`TableCell` take a `className`
   (`ui/table.tsx`), but `DataTable` never reads `column.columnDef.meta` at all. Fixed.
6. **Deferred, not fixed in this step (out of this step's `touches`, flagged for a
   follow-up once the owning steps land):** `date/Input.tsx`'s `DateTimePicker`
   trigger and `richtext/Input.tsx` also set no `aria-invalid`, but fixing them means

   `textarea/Input.tsx` (Step 3) is a brand-new file this step did not touch; it
   shares `text`'s `aria-invalid` gap but is out of this step's declared scope.
7. **Admin links are hand-built at 30 call sites** — every field type's `Cell.tsx` title link
   (16 files), `AdminSidebar.tsx`/`AdminTopNav.tsx` nav and breadcrumbs (7 sites), and
   `DashboardView.tsx`/`GlobalsListView.tsx`/`CollectionListView.tsx`/`MediaCollectionListView.tsx`

```ts
/** Display modes a `select()` field's admin input can render as. */
export const SELECT_DISPLAYS = {
  dropdown: "dropdown",
  radio: "radio",
} as const;

/** `"dropdown" | "radio"` — see {@link SELECT_DISPLAYS}. */
export type SelectDisplay =
  (typeof SELECT_DISPLAYS)[keyof typeof SELECT_DISPLAYS];

/** Per-type `admin` input for `select()` — adds `searchable`/`display` and `condition` (Step 6). */
export interface SelectFieldAdminInput<
  TCollectionSlug extends VexResourceSlug = VexResourceSlug,
> extends FieldAdminConfigInput {
  /**
   * Shows a search box inside the options popover. Only meaningful when
   * `display` is `"dropdown"` (the default) — the `"radio"` display has no
   * popover to search.
   *
   * Default: `false`
   */
  searchable?: boolean;
  /**
   * How the field renders its options.
   *
   * - `"dropdown"` — a searchable-optional popover trigger (`MultiSelect`).
   * - `"radio"` — an inline list with no popover: radio buttons when
   *   `hasMany` is `false`, checkboxes when `hasMany` is `true`.
   *
   * Default: `"dropdown"`
   */
  display?: SelectDisplay;
  condition?(props: FieldConditionProps<TCollectionSlug>): boolean;
}

/** Resolved per-type `admin` for `select()`. */
export interface SelectFieldAdminConfig<
  TCollectionSlug extends VexResourceSlug = VexResourceSlug,
> extends FieldAdminConfig {
  /** Whether the options popover shows a search box (`"dropdown"` display only). */
  searchable: boolean;
  /** How the field renders its options — `"dropdown"` or `"radio"`. */
  display: SelectDisplay;
  condition?(props: FieldConditionProps<TCollectionSlug>): boolean;
}
```

#### packages/react/src/components/form/FormError.tsx

Entire file, replacing the existing implementation (untouched by Steps 1/2/3/6/10) —
`isFieldShowingError` is the same touched/submissionAttempts timing `FormError`
already computed inline, now exported so every field `Input.tsx` can drive its
control's `aria-invalid` off the identical rule the visible message uses, instead
of each type reimplementing it (or, as found above, never implementing it at all).

```tsx
import { TypedFieldApi } from "./createFieldInput";
import { Activity, ComponentPropsWithRef } from "react";
import { cn } from "../../styles/utils";

/**
 * Extracts a field's current validation-error message, if any. TanStack Form
 * v1 stores Standard Schema issue objects in `errors[]`, not strings — this
 * reads `.message` when the error is an object (Zod v4 issues carry
 * `{ origin, code, minimum, inclusive, path, message }`).
 */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
function getFieldErrorMessage(field: TypedFieldApi<any>): string | undefined {
  const rawError = field.state.meta.errors[0];
  return typeof rawError === "string"
    ? rawError
    : (rawError as { message?: string } | undefined)?.message;
}

/**
 * Whether a field should currently present as invalid — touched or a
 * submission has been attempted, and a real error is present. The exact
 * timing `FormError` uses to decide whether to render its message; field
 * inputs call this to set `aria-invalid` on their control so the control's
 * own destructive-ring styling (`ui/input.tsx`, `ui/checkbox.tsx`,
 * `ui/button.tsx`, `ui/multi-select.tsx`) activates in lockstep with the
 * visible message, rather than the message being the only signal.
 */
export function isFieldShowingError(props: {
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  field: TypedFieldApi<any>;
  submissionAttempts: number;
}): boolean {
  const errorMessage = getFieldErrorMessage(props.field);
  return Boolean(
    (props.field.state.meta.isTouched || props.submissionAttempts > 0) &&
    errorMessage,
  );
}

// eslint-disable-next-line jsdoc/require-jsdoc
export function FormError({
  field,
  submissionAttempts,
  className,
  ...pProps
}: {
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  field: TypedFieldApi<any>;
  submissionAttempts: number;
} & ComponentPropsWithRef<"p">) {
  const errorMessage = getFieldErrorMessage(field);
  const showError = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });

  return (
    <Activity mode={showError ? "visible" : "hidden"}>
      <p
        className={cn("text-[0.8rem] text-destructive", className)}
        {...pProps}
      >
        {errorMessage}
      </p>
    </Activity>
  );
}
```

#### packages/react/src/components/fields/text/Input.tsx

Entire file, replacing the Step-10-landed implementation — the render function's
body changes throughout (counter, `aria-invalid`, both-source `disabled` on both
the masked and unmasked `<Input>`), so it is shown complete per the repo
convention.

````tsx
"use client";

import { useContext } from "react";

import { resolveFieldMask, type TextField } from "@vexcms/core";
import { Input } from "../../ui/input";
import { createFieldInput } from "../../form/createFieldInput";
import { FormDescription } from "../../form/FormDescription";
import { FormLabel } from "../../form/FormLabel";
import { FormError, isFieldShowingError } from "../../form/FormError";
import { useFieldMask } from "../../../hooks/useFieldMask";
import { VexConfigContext } from "../../../context/VexConfigContext";

/**
 * Text field input component for the admin edit form.
 *
 * Built with `createFieldInput` — handles TanStack Form wiring automatically.
 * Must be rendered inside `<AppForm>`, or receive an explicit `field` prop
 * (`TypedFieldApi<string>`) from a `<form.Field>` render prop.
 *
 * Renders a masked, uncontrolled `<Input>` when `fieldDef.admin.mask` (or the
 * project's `fields.inputMasks.text` default) resolves, and an unmasked,
 * controlled `<Input>` otherwise — see `useFieldMask`'s JSDoc for why the two
 * cannot share one element.
 *
 * Shows a live `length/max` character counter below the input whenever
 * `fieldDef.max` is set — purely informational, matching `url`/`number`'s own
 * no-client-side-enforcement rule: length limits are still enforced only by
 * `textFieldToInputSchema` at submit time. The same markup is reused by
 * `textarea/Input.tsx`'s own counter.
 *
 * The `name` prop is the field key from the collection config (e.g. `"title"`).
 * It connects the input to the form field with that key in `form.defaultValues`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Inside CollectionEditView — AppForm provides context
 * <AppForm form={form}>
 *   <TextFieldInput name="title" fieldDef={titleField} readOnly={false} />
 * </AppForm>
 *
 * // Explicit field prop — TypedFieldApi<string>, works outside AppForm
 * <form.Field name="title">
 *   {(field) => (
 *     <TextFieldInput
 *       name="title"
 *       fieldDef={titleField}
 *       readOnly={false}
 *       field={field}
 *     />
 *   )}
 * </form.Field>
 * ```
 */
export const TextFieldInput = createFieldInput<string, {}, TextField>(
  ({ name, readOnly, fieldDef, field, index, submissionAttempts }) => {
    const config = useContext(VexConfigContext);
    const mask = resolveFieldMask({
      fieldType: fieldDef.type,
      fieldMask: fieldDef.admin.mask,
      inputMasks: config?.fields.inputMasks ?? {},
    });
    const maskRef = useFieldMask({ mask });
    const value = field.state.value ?? "";
    const isInvalid = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });
    const isDisabled = readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly;
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <FormLabel index={index} field={fieldDef} name={name} />
        {mask ? (
          <Input
            id={name}
            ref={maskRef}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="text"
            defaultValue={value}
            onInput={(e) => field.handleChange(e.currentTarget.value)}
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        ) : (
          <Input
            id={name}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="text"
            value={value}
            onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        )}
        {fieldDef.max && (
          <p className="self-end text-[0.8rem] text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">
            {value.length}/{fieldDef.max[0]}
          </p>
        )}
        <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
        <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
      </div>
    );
  },
);
````

````tsx
"use client";

import { useContext } from "react";

import { resolveFieldMask, type EmailField } from "@vexcms/core";
import { Input } from "../../ui/input";
import { createFieldInput } from "../../form/createFieldInput";
import { FormDescription } from "../../form/FormDescription";
import { FormLabel } from "../../form/FormLabel";
import { FormError, isFieldShowingError } from "../../form/FormError";
import { useFieldMask } from "../../../hooks/useFieldMask";
import { VexConfigContext } from "../../../context/VexConfigContext";

/**
 * Email field input component for the admin edit form.
 *
 * Built with `createFieldInput` — handles TanStack Form wiring automatically.
 * Must be rendered inside `<AppForm>`, or receive an explicit `field` prop
 * (`TypedFieldApi<string>`) from a `<form.Field>` render prop.
 *
 * Renders a masked, uncontrolled `type="text"` `<Input>` when
 * `fieldDef.admin.mask` (or the project's `fields.inputMasks.email` default)
 * resolves, and an unmasked, controlled native `type="email"` `<Input>`
 * otherwise — see `useFieldMask`'s JSDoc for why the two cannot share one
 * element. `autoComplete="email"` is set on both branches.
 *
 * Shows a live `length/max` character counter below the input whenever
 * `fieldDef.max` is set, identical markup to `text/Input.tsx`'s own counter —
 * purely informational; length limits are still enforced only by
 * `emailFieldToInputSchema` at submit time.
 *
 * The `name` prop is the field key from the collection config (e.g. `"contactEmail"`).
 * It connects the input to the form field with that key in `form.defaultValues`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Inside CollectionEditView — AppForm provides context
 * <AppForm form={form}>
 *   <EmailFieldInput name="contactEmail" fieldDef={contactEmailField} readOnly={false} />
 * </AppForm>
 * ```
 */
export const EmailFieldInput = createFieldInput<string, {}, EmailField>(
  ({ name, readOnly, fieldDef, field, index, submissionAttempts }) => {
    const config = useContext(VexConfigContext);
    const mask = resolveFieldMask({
      fieldType: fieldDef.type,
      fieldMask: fieldDef.admin.mask,
      inputMasks: config?.fields.inputMasks ?? {},
    });
    const maskRef = useFieldMask({ mask });
    const value = field.state.value ?? "";
    const isInvalid = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });
    const isDisabled = readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly;
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <FormLabel index={index} field={fieldDef} name={name} />
        {mask ? (
          <Input
            id={name}
            ref={maskRef}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="text"
            autoComplete="email"
            defaultValue={value}
            onInput={(e) => field.handleChange(e.currentTarget.value)}
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        ) : (
          <Input
            id={name}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="email"
            autoComplete="email"
            value={value}
            onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        )}
        {fieldDef.max && (
          <p className="self-end text-[0.8rem] text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">
            {value.length}/{fieldDef.max[0]}
          </p>
        )}
        <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
        <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
      </div>
    );
  },
);
````

#### packages/react/src/components/fields/number/Input.tsx

Entire file, replacing the Step-10-landed implementation. `step`/`min`/`max` HTML
attributes apply only to the unmasked `type="number"` branch — a masked number
renders `type="text"` (Step 10), where `step`/`min`/`max` are inert; `number`'s
`disabled` was already both-source on both branches pre-this-step, so no change
there.

````tsx
"use client";

import { useContext } from "react";

import { resolveFieldMask, type NumberField } from "@vexcms/core";
import { Input } from "../../ui/input";
import { createFieldInput } from "../../form/createFieldInput";
import { FormDescription } from "../../form/FormDescription";
import { FormLabel } from "../../form/FormLabel";
import { FormError, isFieldShowingError } from "../../form/FormError";
import { useFieldMask } from "../../../hooks/useFieldMask";
import { VexConfigContext } from "../../../context/VexConfigContext";

/**
 * Number field input component for the admin edit form.
 *
 * Built with `createFieldInput` — handles TanStack Form wiring automatically.
 * Must be rendered inside `<AppForm>`, or receive an explicit `field` prop
 * (`TypedFieldApi<number>`) from a `<form.Field>` render prop.
 *
 * Renders a masked, uncontrolled `type="text"` `<Input>` when
 * `fieldDef.admin.mask` (or the project's `fields.inputMasks.number` default)
 * resolves — still storing a `number` — and an unmasked, controlled
 * `type="number"` `<Input>` otherwise.
 *
 * `fieldDef.step`/`fieldDef.min`/`fieldDef.max` are forwarded as the native
 * `step`/`min`/`max` HTML attributes on the unmasked branch only — UI
 * affordances (spinner increment, browser validity styling), never
 * client-side clamping; range enforcement stays entirely in
 * `numberFieldToInputSchema`.
 *
 * The `name` prop is the field key from the collection config (e.g. `"price"`).
 * It connects the input to the form field with that key in `form.defaultValues`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Inside CollectionEditView — AppForm provides context
 * <AppForm form={form}>
 *   <NumberFieldInput name="price" fieldDef={priceField} readOnly={false} />
 * </AppForm>
 * ```
 */
export const NumberFieldInput = createFieldInput<number, {}, NumberField>(
  ({ name, readOnly, fieldDef, field, index, submissionAttempts }) => {
    const config = useContext(VexConfigContext);
    const mask = resolveFieldMask({
      fieldType: fieldDef.type,
      fieldMask: fieldDef.admin.mask,
      inputMasks: config?.fields.inputMasks ?? {},
    });
    const maskRef = useFieldMask({ mask });
    const isInvalid = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });
    const isDisabled = readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly;
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <FormLabel field={fieldDef} index={index} name={name} />
        {mask ? (
          <Input
            id={name}
            ref={maskRef}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="text"
            defaultValue={
              field.state.value !== undefined ? String(field.state.value) : ""
            }
            onInput={(e) => {
              const raw = e.currentTarget.value;
              field.handleChange(
                raw === "" ? (undefined as unknown as number) : Number(raw),
              );
            }}
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        ) : (
          <Input
            id={name}
            disabled={isDisabled}
            type="number"
            step={fieldDef.step}
            min={fieldDef.min?.[0]}
            max={fieldDef.max?.[0]}
            value={field.state.value ?? 0}
            onChange={(e) =>
              field.handleChange(
                e.target.value === ""
                  ? (undefined as unknown as number)
                  : Number(e.target.value),
              )
            }
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
            readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
          />
        )}
        <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
        <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
      </div>
    );
  },
);
````

#### packages/react/src/components/fields/url/Input.tsx

Entire file, replacing the Step-10-landed implementation. The open-link button
sits outside the mask branch — it reads `field.state.value` directly, which
stays the live, reactive form value in both the masked (uncontrolled DOM,
`onInput` still calls `field.handleChange`) and unmasked cases.

````tsx
"use client";

import { useContext } from "react";
import { resolveFieldMask, type UrlField } from "@vexcms/core";
import { Input } from "../../ui/input";
import { Button } from "../../ui/button";
import { VexLink } from "../../ui/VexLink";
import { createFieldInput } from "../../form/createFieldInput";
import { FormDescription } from "../../form/FormDescription";
import { FormLabel } from "../../form/FormLabel";
import { FormError, isFieldShowingError } from "../../form/FormError";
import { useFieldMask } from "../../../hooks/useFieldMask";
import { VexConfigContext } from "../../../context/VexConfigContext";

/**
 * Whether `value` parses as an absolute URL (`new URL()` succeeds). Used only
 * to enable/disable the open-link button below — format validation for
 * submission stays entirely in `urlFieldToInputSchema`, never here.
 */
function isParseableUrl(value: string): boolean {
  if (!value) return false;
  try {
    new URL(value);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * URL field input component for the admin edit form.
 *
 * Renders a masked, uncontrolled `<Input>` when `fieldDef.admin.mask` (or the
 * project's `fields.inputMasks.url` default) resolves, and an unmasked,
 * controlled `<Input type="text">` otherwise — URL format validation is
 * handled by `urlFieldToInputSchema` at submit time either way, never by the
 * browser's built-in `type="url"` input. Built with `createFieldInput`, which
 * handles TanStack Form wiring automatically.
 *
 * An open-link button sits beside the input, enabled only while the current
 * value parses as an absolute URL (`isParseableUrl`); it opens the value in a
 * new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
 *
 * Must be rendered inside `<AppForm>`, or receive an explicit `field` prop
 * (`TypedFieldApi<string>`) from a `<form.Field>` render prop.
 *
 * The `name` prop is the field key from the collection config (e.g. `"website"`).
 * It connects the input to the form field with that key in `form.defaultValues`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Inside CollectionEditView — AppForm provides context
 * <AppForm form={form}>
 *   <UrlFieldInput name="website" fieldDef={websiteField} readOnly={false} />
 * </AppForm>
 * ```
 */
export const UrlFieldInput = createFieldInput<string, {}, UrlField>(
  ({ name, readOnly, fieldDef, field, index, submissionAttempts }) => {
    const config = useContext(VexConfigContext);
    const mask = resolveFieldMask({
      fieldType: fieldDef.type,
      fieldMask: fieldDef.admin.mask,
      inputMasks: config?.fields.inputMasks ?? {},
    });
    const maskRef = useFieldMask({ mask });
    const value = field.state.value ?? "";
    const isValidUrl = isParseableUrl(value);
    const isInvalid = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });
    const isDisabled = readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly;
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <FormLabel field={fieldDef} index={index} name={name} />
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          {mask ? (
            <Input
              id={name}
              ref={maskRef}
              type="text"
              disabled={isDisabled}
              defaultValue={value}
              onInput={(e) => field.handleChange(e.currentTarget.value)}
              onBlur={field.handleBlur}
              placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
              readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
              aria-required={fieldDef.required}
              aria-invalid={isInvalid}
            />
          ) : (
            <Input
              id={name}
              type="text"
              disabled={isDisabled}
              value={value}
              onChange={(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value)}
              onBlur={field.handleBlur}
              placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder}
              readOnly={fieldDef.admin.readOnly}
              aria-required={fieldDef.required}
              aria-invalid={isInvalid}
            />
          )}
          <Button
            type="button"
            variant="outline"
            size="icon"
            nativeButton={false}
            disabled={!isValidUrl}
            aria-label="Open link in new tab"
            icon="ExternalLink"
            iconPosition="center"
            render={
              <VexLink
                href={isValidUrl ? value : ""}
                target="_blank"
                rel="noopener noreferrer"
              />
            }
          />
        </div>
        <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
        <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
      </div>
    );
  },
);
````

**P-023 correction (implementation-discovered):** `VexLinkProps.href` (`hooks/useFrameworkComponents.ts`)
is `string`, not `string | undefined` — the code block above uses `href={isValidUrl ? value : ""}`,
not `: undefined`, which fails `tsc` (`Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type
'string'.`). The empty-string fallback is inert: the `Button`'s own `disabled={!isValidUrl}`
already prevents the render-prop `VexLink` from being reachable while `isValidUrl` is `false`.


#### packages/react/src/components/ui/radio-group.tsx

New file. Mirrors `ui/checkbox.tsx`'s pattern — styled wrappers directly on Base UI's
`RadioGroup`/`Radio.Root`/`Radio.Indicator`, no new abstraction layer (Design Decision 32).
Used below by `select/Input.tsx`'s `admin.display: "radio"` branch when `hasMany` is `false`.

```tsx
import { Radio as RadioPrimitive, RadioGroup as RadioGroupPrimitive } from "@base-ui/react";

import { cn } from "../../styles/utils";

/** Styled radio group built on Base UI `RadioGroup`, sharing selection state across its `RadioGroupItem` children. */
function RadioGroup({ className, ...props }: RadioGroupPrimitive.Props) {
  return (
    <RadioGroupPrimitive
      data-slot="radio-group"
      className={cn("flex flex-col gap-2", className)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}

/** Styled radio button built on Base UI `Radio.Root` with a filled-dot `Radio.Indicator`. */
function RadioGroupItem({ className, ...props }: RadioPrimitive.Root.Props) {
  return (
    <RadioPrimitive.Root
      data-slot="radio-group-item"
      className={cn(
        "relative flex size-4 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-input shadow-xs transition-shadow outline-none group-has-disabled/field:opacity-50 focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 aria-invalid:border-destructive aria-invalid:ring-3 aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20 dark:bg-input/30 dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40 data-checked:border-primary",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      <RadioPrimitive.Indicator
        data-slot="radio-group-item-indicator"
        className="size-2 rounded-full bg-primary"
      />
    </RadioPrimitive.Root>
  );
}

export { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem };
```

#### packages/react/src/components/fields/select/Input.tsx

Entire file, replacing the existing implementation. `select` is untouched by
Steps 1/2/3/10. Step 11 (`g-step-11.md:1835-1841`) makes one isolated edit to the
pre-this-step file — the JSDoc line `Fields are rendered generically by
\`RenderFieldInputComponents\`, so there is` → `` `RenderFields`, so there is ``
(`RenderFieldInputComponents`is removed in Step 11). This full-file rewrite
already carries the post-Step-11 wording verbatim in its JSDoc below (see
"Fields are rendered generically by`RenderFields`, so there is no prop
channel…"), so no further re-anchoring is needed — the entire-file replacement
subsumes Step 11's one-line edit.

````tsx
"use client";

import { SELECT_DISPLAYS, type SelectField } from "@vexcms/core";
import { useModalSurface } from "../../../hooks/useModalSurface";
import { createFieldInput } from "../../form/createFieldInput";
import { FormDescription } from "../../form/FormDescription";
import { FormLabel } from "../../form/FormLabel";
import { FormError, isFieldShowingError } from "../../form/FormError";
import { Checkbox } from "../../ui/checkbox";
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "../../ui/radio-group";
import {
  MultiSelect,
  MultiSelectContent,
  MultiSelectGroup,
  MultiSelectItem,
  MultiSelectTrigger,
  MultiSelectValue,
} from "../../ui/multi-select";

/**
 * Select field input component for the admin edit form.
 *
 * Built with `createFieldInput` — handles TanStack Form wiring automatically.
 * Must be rendered inside `<AppForm>`, or receive an explicit `field` prop
 * (`TypedFieldApi<string[]>`) from a `<form.Field>` render prop.
 *
 * The `name` prop is the field key from the collection config (e.g. `"status"`).
 * It connects the input to the form field with that key in `form.defaultValues`.
 * When `fieldDef.hasMany` is `false`, only one option may be selected at a time.
 *
 * `fieldDef.admin.display` picks the rendering: the default `"dropdown"` is a
 * popover (`MultiSelect`), optionally searchable via `fieldDef.admin.searchable`;
 * `"radio"` renders an inline list with no popover — radio buttons when
 * `hasMany` is `false`, checkboxes when `hasMany` is `true` — and ignores
 * `searchable`, which only applies to the popover.
 *
 * Fields are rendered generically by `RenderFields`, so there is no prop
 * channel to tell this input it sits in a dialog. It reads `useModalSurface()`
 * instead, which `Modal` provides: inside a dialog the popover joins that
 * surface's focus trap, and everywhere else it stays non-modal so it does not
 * lock page scroll and snap the view to the top. Only the `"dropdown"` display
 * has a popover to apply this to.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * // Inside CollectionEditView — AppForm provides context
 * <AppForm form={form}>
 *   <SelectFieldInput name="status" fieldDef={statusField} readOnly={false} />
 * </AppForm>
 *
 * // Explicit field prop — TypedFieldApi<string[]>, works outside AppForm
 * <form.Field name="tags">
 *   {(field) => (
 *     <SelectFieldInput
 *       name="tags"
 *       fieldDef={tagsField}
 *       readOnly={false}
 *       field={field}
 *     />
 *   )}
 * </form.Field>
 * ```
 */
export const SelectFieldInput = createFieldInput<string[], {}, SelectField>(
  ({ name, readOnly, fieldDef, field, index, submissionAttempts }) => {
    const isOnModalSurface = useModalSurface();
    const isReadOnly = readOnly || fieldDef.admin.readOnly;
    const isInvalid = isFieldShowingError({ field, submissionAttempts });

    function handleOptionToggle(value: string) {
      const current = field.state.value ?? [];
      if (fieldDef.hasMany) {
        field.handleChange(
          current.includes(value)
            ? current.filter((v) => v !== value)
            : [...current, value],
        );
      } else {
        field.handleChange(current.includes(value) ? [] : [value]);
      }
    }

    if (fieldDef.admin.display === SELECT_DISPLAYS.radio) {
      return (
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
          <span
            id={`${name}-label`}
            className="relative flex items-center gap-2 text-sm leading-none font-medium select-none group-data-[disabled=true]:pointer-events-none group-data-[disabled=true]:opacity-50 peer-disabled:cursor-not-allowed peer-disabled:opacity-50"
          >
            {index !== undefined ? `[${index + 1}] - ` : ""}
            {fieldDef.label || name}
            {fieldDef.required && <span className="text-red-500">*</span>}
          </span>
          {fieldDef.hasMany ? (
            <div
              role="group"
              aria-labelledby={`${name}-label`}
              aria-disabled={isReadOnly}
              className="flex flex-col gap-2"
            >
              {fieldDef.options.map((option, optionIndex) => (
                <label
                  key={`${name}-option-${optionIndex}`}
                  className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm"
                >
                  <Checkbox
                    checked={(field.state.value ?? []).includes(option.value)}
                    disabled={isReadOnly}
                    onCheckedChange={() => handleOptionToggle(option.value)}
                    onBlur={field.handleBlur}
                    aria-invalid={isInvalid}
                    aria-label={option.label}
                  />
                  {option.label}
                </label>
              ))}
            </div>
          ) : (
            <RadioGroup
              aria-labelledby={`${name}-label`}
              disabled={isReadOnly}
              value={(field.state.value ?? [])[0]}
              onValueChange={(value) => field.handleChange([value as string])}
              onBlur={field.handleBlur}
              className="gap-2"
            >
              {fieldDef.options.map((option, optionIndex) => (
                <label
                  key={`${name}-option-${optionIndex}`}
                  className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm"
                >
                  <RadioGroupItem
                    value={option.value}
                    aria-invalid={isInvalid}
                    aria-label={option.label}
                  />
                  {option.label}
                </label>
              ))}
            </RadioGroup>
          )}
          <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
          <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
        </div>
      );
    }

    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-1.5">
        <FormLabel field={fieldDef} index={index} name={name} />
        <MultiSelect
          modal={isOnModalSurface}
          onValuesChange={field.handleChange}
          single={!fieldDef.hasMany}
          values={field.state.value}
        >
          <MultiSelectTrigger
            id={name}
            className="w-full"
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            name={name}
            aria-required={fieldDef.required}
            aria-invalid={isInvalid}
            disabled={isReadOnly}
          >
            <MultiSelectValue placeholder={fieldDef.admin.placeholder} />
          </MultiSelectTrigger>
          <MultiSelectContent
            onBlur={field.handleBlur}
            className="w-full"
            search={fieldDef.admin.searchable}
          >
            <MultiSelectGroup>
              {fieldDef.options.map((o, i) => (
                <MultiSelectItem
                  value={o.value}
                  key={`multi-select-item-${name}-${i}`}
                >
                  {o.label}
                </MultiSelectItem>
              ))}
            </MultiSelectGroup>
          </MultiSelectContent>
        </MultiSelect>
        <FormDescription field={fieldDef} />
        <FormError field={field} submissionAttempts={submissionAttempts} />
      </div>
    );
  },
);
````

**P-023 correction (implementation-discovered):** the `Checkbox`/`RadioGroupItem` controls
above carry an explicit `aria-label={option.label}` not present in an earlier draft of this
block. Without it, wrapping the control in a `<label>…{option.label}</label>` does not give
the Base UI styled `role="checkbox"`/`role="radio"` `<span>` an accessible name — native
implicit label association only applies to real labelable HTML elements (`<input>`,
`<button>`, …), not an ARIA-role `<span>` — so `getByRole(..., { name: option.label })`
found zero matches. Fixed by adding `aria-label` directly to both controls (code block above
already reflects the fix).

Separately, `Input.test.tsx`'s `"selects a single value by clicking its radio…"` and
`"accumulates checked values by clicking multiple checkboxes…"` tests must click the hidden
native `<input type="radio"|"checkbox">` rendered inside each Base UI control, not the
visible `role="radio"`/`role="checkbox"` `<span>` — the same jsdom `PointerEvent` gap
`dataTableSuite.tsx`'s checkbox-column test and `checkbox/Input.test.tsx` already document
(Base UI's click handler on the visible span throws `ReferenceError: PointerEvent is not
defined` under jsdom). Query `container.querySelectorAll('input[type="radio"]')` /
`'input[type="checkbox"]'` and click the entry at the clicked option's index instead of
`screen.getByRole("radio"/"checkbox", { name })`.

```ts
/**
 * `ColumnDef.meta`'s actual shape in this package — every `*FieldToColumnDef`
 * factory (`components/fields/<type>/columnDef.tsx`) sets `label`/`align`/
 * `isTitleField`, read back through this local type since the library's own
 * `ColumnMeta` is an empty interface this package never augments.
 */
interface DataTableColumnMeta {
  align?: Alignment;
}

/** Tailwind text-alignment class per {@link Alignment}, applied to both the header and data cells of a column. */
const ALIGNMENT_CLASS: Record<Alignment, string> = {
  left: "text-left",
  right: "text-right",
  center: "text-center",
};
```

    <TableHead
      key={header.id}
      className={
        ALIGNMENT_CLASS[
          (header.column.columnDef.meta as DataTableColumnMeta | undefined)
            ?.align ?? "left"
        ]
      }
    >
      {flexRender(header.column.columnDef.header, header.getContext())}
    </TableHead>
  ));
}

**4 — the body row's `<TableCell>`: apply the same alignment class.**

```tsx
{
  row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
    <TableCell
      key={cell.id}
      className={
        ALIGNMENT_CLASS[
          (cell.column.columnDef.meta as DataTableColumnMeta | undefined)
            ?.align ?? "left"
        ]
      }
    >
      {flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell, cell.getContext())}
    </TableCell>
  ));
}
```

#### packages/react/src/utils/adminHref.ts

New file.

````ts
import { addLeadingSlash } from "@vexcms/core";
import { MODALS } from "../components/modals/constants";

/**
 * Target an admin panel URL points at — the one discriminated union every
 * hand-built `${basePath}/...` string in this package is replaced with.
 *
 * `"create"` is not a separate route: creating a document opens a modal on
 * the collection's own list view (`CollectionListView`), so it resolves to
 * the SAME path as `"collection"` plus the create-modal's `nuqs` query
 * param. Media's own "Upload" action uses a DIFFERENT modal
 * (`MODALS.uploadMedia`) and is left to its call site to append — `"create"`
 * only knows about `MODALS.createDocument`.
 */
export type AdminHrefTarget =
  | { type: "dashboard" }
  | { type: "collection"; slug: string }
  | { type: "global"; slug: string }
  | { type: "document"; slug: string; id: string }
  | { type: "create"; slug: string };

/**
 * Builds an admin panel URL from a target and the project's configured
 * `basePath` — the one place every admin link in `@vexcms/react` (and, via
 * re-export, `@vexcms/next`) computes a path. Replaces 30 hand-built
 * `` `${basePath}/...` `` / hardcoded `"/admin/..."` call sites across the
 * nav, breadcrumb, dashboard, list views, and all 16 field types' `Cell.tsx`
 * title links (Step 17 audit finding 7) — grep for `adminHref(` to confirm
 * no hand-built admin URL remains outside this file.
 *
 * URL shape is UNCHANGED from what every call site already produced —
 * `/{basePath}/{slug}`, `/{basePath}/globals/{slug}`,
 * `/{basePath}/{slug}/{id}`. Launch spec H moves collections to
 * `/admin/collections/<slug>`; once it lands, that change is a one-file edit
 * here (plus the route parser `NextAdminLayoutClient.tsx` reads pathname
 * segments from — a separate, pre-existing concern this function does not
 * touch) instead of a 30-site grep.
 *
 * @param target - What the link points at.
 * @param basePath - The project's configured `VexClientConfig.basePath`
 *   (e.g. `config.basePath`), leading-slash-normalized internally via
 *   `addLeadingSlash` the same way every replaced call site already did.
 * @returns The absolute admin panel path for `target`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * adminHref({ type: "dashboard" }, "/admin");                          // "/admin"
 * adminHref({ type: "collection", slug: "posts" }, "/admin");          // "/admin/posts"
 * adminHref({ type: "global", slug: "siteSettings" }, "/admin");       // "/admin/globals/siteSettings"
 * adminHref({ type: "document", slug: "posts", id: "abc" }, "/admin"); // "/admin/posts/abc"
 * adminHref({ type: "create", slug: "posts" }, "/admin");              // "/admin/posts?createNew=true"
 * ```
 */
export function adminHref(target: AdminHrefTarget, basePath: string): string {
  const root = addLeadingSlash(basePath);
  switch (target.type) {
    case "dashboard":
      return root;
    case "collection":
      return `${root}/${target.slug}`;
    case "global":
      return `${root}/globals/${target.slug}`;
    case "document":
      return `${root}/${target.slug}/${target.id}`;
    case "create":
      return `${root}/${target.slug}?${MODALS.createDocument.urlParam}=true`;
  }
}
````

**Design note — why `@vexcms/react`, not `@vexcms/core`.** `adminHref`'s path-joining is itself
framework- and React-agnostic (`addLeadingSlash` plus template-literal joins), but the `"create"`
variant's query-param convention is owned by `MODALS` (`components/modals/constants.ts`), a
`@vexcms/react`-only concept — core has no notion of a `nuqs`-driven modal. Splitting `adminHref`
across packages (path-joining in core, the `"create"` case layered on top in react) would turn one
function into two for a function whose only non-trivial case already needs react's own constant;
kept as one function in `@vexcms/react`.

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { adminHref } from "./adminHref";
import { MODALS } from "../components/modals/constants";

describe("adminHref", () => {
  it("builds the dashboard URL", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "dashboard" }, "/admin")).toBe("/admin");
  });

  it("builds a collection list URL", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "collection", slug: "posts" }, "/admin")).toBe(
      "/admin/posts",
    );
  });

  it("builds a global edit URL", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "global", slug: "siteSettings" }, "/admin")).toBe(
      "/admin/globals/siteSettings",
    );
  });

  it("builds a document edit URL", () => {
    expect(
      adminHref({ type: "document", slug: "posts", id: "abc123" }, "/admin"),
    ).toBe("/admin/posts/abc123");
  });

  it("builds a create-modal URL, reusing MODALS.createDocument's own urlParam", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "create", slug: "posts" }, "/admin")).toBe(
      `/admin/posts?${MODALS.createDocument.urlParam}=true`,
    );
  });

  it("normalizes a basePath without a leading slash, matching addLeadingSlash", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "collection", slug: "posts" }, "admin")).toBe(
      "/admin/posts",
    );
  });

  it("supports a custom basePath", () => {
    expect(adminHref({ type: "collection", slug: "posts" }, "/cms")).toBe(
      "/cms/posts",
    );
  });
});

#### packages/react/src/components/fields/text/Cell.tsx (representative — all 16 field `Cell.tsx` files)

**1 — import.** Add `adminHref` alongside the existing `addLeadingSlash` import:

```ts

  adminHref,
  type CellComponentProps,
  type TextField,
} from "@vexcms/core";

```

(`addLeadingSlash`/`config.basePath` destructuring is DROPPED — `adminHref` takes `config.basePath`
directly, so the `const basePath = addLeadingSlash(config.basePath);` line every one of these 16

**2 — the href itself,** anchored at `` `${basePath}/${props.collection.slug}/${props.row.original._id}` ``
(or, for `email`/`url`, the ternary branch using the same template literal):

```ts
adminHref(
  { type: "document", slug: props.collection.slug, id: props.row.original._id },
  config.basePath,
);
```

Identical two-edit change (drop the `basePath` local, replace the template literal with one
`adminHref(...)` call) applies to all 16 field types' `Cell.tsx`, same anchor pattern in each —
`array`, `blocks`, `checkbox`, `color`, `date`, `email`, `group`, `json`, `number`,
`relationship`, `richtext`, `select`, `text`, `textarea`, `upload`, `url`. `email/Cell.tsx` and
`url/Cell.tsx` keep their ternary (`mailto:`/raw URL on the non-title branch) — only the
title-field branch's template literal changes. `relationship/Cell.tsx` and `upload/Cell.tsx`
already hoist `href` into a local above their `wrap` helper; same substitution, same local name.

#### apps/test/src/vexcms/admin/WordCountField.tsx

New file — the `apps/test`-local `Field` component for the `ui()` dogfood field below.

```tsx
"use client";

import type { UIFieldComponentProps } from "@vexcms/core";

/** Live word count of the page's `content` field — dogfoods `ui()` (Step 6): no stored value, read-only derived display. */
export function WordCountField(props: UIFieldComponentProps) {
  const content = typeof props.data.content === "string" ? props.data.content : "";
  const words = content.trim().length === 0 ? 0 : content.trim().split(/\s+/).length;
  return (
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
      {props.name}: {words} word{words === 1 ? "" : "s"}
    </p>
  );
}
```

#### apps/test/src/vexcms/blocks/CTA/index.tsx

Anchored edit replacing the `href={action.href}` line. `internalPage`'s stored value is
always `Id<"pages">[]` (relationship's generated `interfaceType`, regardless of `hasMany`
— `packages/core/src/fields/relationship/config.ts`), so the first id is the target.

**Edit — add `resolveHref` above the component and use it in the `Link`:**

```tsx
function resolveHref(action: NonNullable<CtaBlock["actions"]>[number]): string {
  if (action.linkType?.[0] === "internal") {
    return `/${action.internalPage?.[0] ?? ""}`;
  }
  return action.externalUrl ?? "#";
}

export default function CTABlock({ block }: BlockComponentProps) {
  const { actions, heading, subheading } = block as CtaBlock;
  const items = actions ?? [];

  return (
    <section className="border-y border-border bg-card py-16 text-center md:py-24 xl:py-32">
      <Container>
        <h2 className="mx-auto max-w-[24ch] text-[28px] leading-[1.12] font-bold tracking-[-0.03em] text-balance text-foreground md:text-4xl xl:text-[40px]">
          {heading}
        </h2>

        {subheading ? (
          <p className="mx-auto mt-5 max-w-[60ch] text-[17px] leading-[1.6] text-pretty text-muted-foreground">
            {subheading}
          </p>
        ) : null}

        {items.length > 0 ? (
          <div className="mx-auto mt-9 flex w-full max-w-[320px] flex-col gap-3 sm:max-w-none sm:flex-row sm:flex-wrap sm:justify-center">
            {items.map((action, index) => (
              <Link
                className={cn(
                  buttonVariants({
                    size: "lg",
                    variant: index === 0 ? "default" : "outline",
                  }),
                  "active:translate-y-px",
                )}
                href={resolveHref(action)}
                key={`${action.label}-${index}`}
              >
                {action.label}
              </Link>
            ))}
          </div>
        ) : null}
      </Container>
    </section>
  );
}
```

   confirm the error message is the value-aware default, not a stale `{ value, error }`
   render.
2. **Step 2 (email)** — open the Advanced tab, type an invalid value into Contact Email
   (e.g. `not-an-email`), confirm a format error; save a valid address, confirm the list
   view and any email-field cell render a `mailto:` link.
3. **Step 3 (textarea)** — type into Internal Notes past 2000 characters; confirm the
   character counter and the max-length error; confirm `rows` renders a 6-row textarea.
4. **Step 4 (json)** — type invalid JSON into Custom Data; confirm a parse-error state
   and that the last valid value is NOT submitted; type valid JSON, save, reload, confirm
   the cell shows a truncated one-line preview.
5. **Step 5 (dates)** — open any existing page, confirm the sidebar shows a read-only
   "Updated At" with date **and** time, plus a separate read-only "Created at" from
   `DocumentTimestamps`.
6. **Step 6/11 (layout)** — confirm the edit view renders "Content" / "SEO" / "Advanced"
   tabs with the URL reflecting `?tab=` on the top-level group; switch tabs and confirm
   state persists on reload; confirm Meta Title / Meta Description render side-by-side at
   roughly 60/40 width in the sidebar and stack below the `sm` breakpoint (narrow the
   browser); expand/collapse "Legacy Test Fields".
7. **Step 9/12 (conditions)** — in a CTA block action, toggle Link Type: selecting
   "External URL" shows only External URL; selecting "Internal Page" shows only Internal
   Page and hides External URL without losing the other field's typed value; submit with
   an empty required field under the hidden branch and confirm no validation error blocks
   save.
8. **Step 10 (masks)** — type into Contact Phone, confirm it masks as `(999) 999-9999`
   while typing; add a `number` field value elsewhere (or use an existing number field)
   and confirm it now masks as `999-999-9999` via the project-wide default from
   `fields.inputMasks.number`, while still storing/submitting a plain number.
9. **Step 13 (search/upload)** — open the OG Image or Test Image upload picker, type a
   search query, confirm results page via "Load more" and the MIME filter matches
   `accept: "image/*"`.
10. **Step 14 (relationship)** — on the CTA action's Internal Page relationship (visible
    with Link Type = Internal Page), open the picker; confirm Select/Create tabs, that a
    created page is auto-selected, and the Themes relationship on the page itself shows
    consistent empty/filled states.
11. **Step 15/16 (blocks)** — on the page's `blocks` field, duplicate a block, insert
    above/below, move up/down, collapse/expand all, then copy a block and paste it above
    in a different block field or a different document tab; confirm pasted ids are fresh
    and unknown keys are dropped if pasting into a different block type.
12. **Step 17 (polish)** — confirm Contact Phone's character counter (if `max` set)
    matches `max`; confirm any `number` field shows `step`/min/max HTML attributes via
    browser devtools; confirm a `url` field (e.g. External URL) shows an open-link button;
    confirm the `linkType` select's `admin.display`/`admin.searchable` (if configured)
    render correctly; confirm `DataTable` column alignment matches each column's
    `cellAlignment`.

## G — Field input consistency pass

> **Re-scoped 2026-10-16** in the dev-spec interview — spec
> `2026-10-16-field-input-consistency-pass`. Absorbs H's block-editing items
> (duplicate/insert/move/collapse-all, per-block actions) and the previously

> layout helpers; see the 16-step task list for the full breakdown.

Every field type has an input and a cell component
(`react/src/components/fields/index.tsx:45-276`), but quality is uneven.

### Scope

- **`relationship`** is the named offender: unlike the media picker it has no
  consistent picker surface, no loading states, and looks rudimentary. Copied from
  upload's three-state pattern, not shared code.
- Sweep all 16 inputs (12 original + richtext from D + the new `email`/`textarea`/`json`)
  for: loading/pending states, empty states, error display, keyboard access, focus rings,
  disabled/read-only rendering, and `admin.placeholder` / `admin.width` /
  `admin.cellAlignment` honoring.
- Add the server-only async validation error path from F.
- **MIME filter in the media library grid** — `MediaLibaryGrid.tsx:36` carries a
  TODO and `upload()` already accepts `accept` (`fields/upload/config.ts:6-40`),
  so the field declares a constraint the picker ignores.
- **Conditional fields (`admin.condition`)** — a pure predicate, same function on client
  and server; hidden fields keep their values and skip `required`/`validate()` server-side.
  `linkType: internal | external` is the canonical use case.
- **Layout**: `width` becomes any CSS width string; `tabs()` / `collapsible()` / `row()`
  layout helpers, flat-record, usable anywhere a fields record is.
- **Masks**: opt-in `admin.mask` + project-wide `fields.inputMasks` defaults.
- **Blocks/array editing**: per-block menu (duplicate, insert above/below, move up/down,
  delete), collapse/expand all, error markers, `n/max` counters, and a clipboard
  (copy/paste blocks across fields, documents, and collections via `localStorage`).

**Acceptance:** every input renders correct empty / loading / error / read-only
states; the a11y assertions already in the field suites extended to cover them; no
field visually inconsistent with its siblings; `apps/test` dogfoods every new field,
layout helper, condition, and block-editing action end-to-end.

## H — Edit-view overhaul

### Scope

- **Unsaved-changes navigation guard.** Dirty state currently only disables the
  Save button (`CollectionEditView.tsx:63-73`); nothing blocks navigating away.
  Losing work on a misclick is the worst first impression per line of code saved.
- **Duplicate document** — absent from every edit view; trivial against existing
  `create`.
- Validation error summary at document level, jump-to-field.
- Keep the sticky header work already landed.

**Out of scope:** concurrent-edit conflict resolution. Already specified in
`backlog.md` ("Concurrent-edit conflict-resolution UX") as three separable pieces
with a design; it needs its own spec and is not a 0.1.0 gate. Duplicate block and the
other block-editing patterns moved to G, 2026-10-16 — `blocks`' per-block actions and
the multi-field editing surface are field-input concerns, not edit-view chrome.

**Acceptance:** navigating away from a dirty form prompts; duplicating a document
works and is covered by `viewSuite`.

#### apps/test/src/vex.config.ts

New section after the `editor` key — a root-level per-type `Input` override demonstrating
S1/S7/S8: a thin wrapper around the built-in `text` input that uppercases its own
`placeholder`, composed via `renderDefault` so the real built-in still renders everything
else unchanged.

```ts
import { UppercasePlaceholderTextInput } from "./vexcms/admin/UppercasePlaceholderTextInput";

// …inside defineConfig({ … })
admin: {
  components: {
    fields: {
      text: {
        Input: { id: "acme.text.uppercasePlaceholder", component: UppercasePlaceholderTextInput },
      },
    },
  },
},
```

```tsx
// apps/test/src/vexcms/admin/UppercasePlaceholderTextInput.tsx
"use client";

import type { TextField, VexResourceSlug } from "@vexcms/core";
import type { ReactHKT } from "@vexcms/react";
import type { SlotOverrideProps } from "@vexcms/react";
import type { InputComponentProps } from "@vexcms/core";

export function UppercasePlaceholderTextInput(
  props: SlotOverrideProps<
    ReactHKT,
    InputComponentProps<{}, TextField<VexResourceSlug>>
  >,
) {
  const { renderDefault, ...rest } = props;
  const RenderDefault = renderDefault;
  return (
    <RenderDefault
      {...rest}
      fieldDef={{
        ...rest.fieldDef,
        admin: {
          ...rest.fieldDef.admin,
          placeholder: rest.fieldDef.admin.placeholder?.toUpperCase(),
        },
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Dogfooded against `pages.ts`'s existing `text()` fields — no field opts in individually; the
root per-type override applies to every `text` field project-wide, proving S1's "root level"
composes with step 11's renderer without a single field author having to know it exists.

#### Implementation notes (fixes found while dogfooding)

1. **Readable keys are `getDataFields` keys.** `CollectionEditView`/`GlobalEditView`/
   `MediaCollectionEditView` call `useVisibleFields` over a memoized `getDataFields({ fields })`
   instead of raw `fields`. Raw top-level keys named containers (`layoutTabs`), never their
   hoisted children (`displayName`, `priceLabel`), so with any discriminating read permission —
   including admin's `"*": true` — every hoisted field was missing from the form AND from
   `readableFields`' form values/validation.
2. **`visibleFieldEntries` gates by data key.** A data field matches `fieldKeys` by its own key;
   a `tabs`/`collapsible`/`row` container renders only while it has a readable descendant; a NAMED
   tab matches by its `name` (`isTabVisible`) and its own fields render with `fieldKeys:
   undefined`, like a group's; a `ui()` field always renders. Any entry with `admin.hidden` —
   container or data — is dropped.
3. **Container `admin` is honored on the render side.** `isFieldVisible` walks
   `getDataFields(fields)`, so a container's and each tab's `admin.condition` (AND-ed) and
   `admin.hidden` (OR-ed) count — the same rules the server sees (decision 13). `useFieldVisible`
   became `useFieldSetsVisible({ fieldSets }) => boolean[]`, one store subscription with an
   element-wise compare; `FormRow`/`FormCollapsible` (now taking `fieldKey`) pass
   `[{ [fieldKey]: field }]`; `FormTabs` passes one set per tab, drops tabs whose set is hidden,
   and falls back to the default tab when `?<fieldKey>=` names a hidden one. `renderField` ORs a
   UI field's `admin.readOnly` into the context its contents render with, and gates `ui()` through
   `FieldConditionGate`.
4. **`RenderFields`' region partition reads `field.admin.position` for every field**, so a
   `ui()` with `position: "sidebar"` renders in the sidebar (it was hard-coded to main).
5. **Sticky sidebar.** The edit-view sidebar column is `sm:sticky sm:top-0 sm:self-start
   sm:max-h-[100cqh] sm:overflow-y-auto`; both form scrollers set `container-type: size`, so
   `100cqh` is the scroller's content-box height. The sidebar stays in view while the form
   scrolls and scrolls on its own when taller than the viewport.
6. **Scroll anchoring off in the admin.** `.vex-scroll-area` sets `overflow-anchor: none`:
   reordering a hasMany relationship (or any dnd list) moved the anchored row and the form
   scroller followed it (measured +128px for a two-row move; 0 after).
7. **Row widths account for the gap.** `FieldLayoutItem` sets a `%` width as
   `calc(<w>% - 1rem * (1 - w))`, so siblings summing to 100% fit beside the `gap-4` gutters
   instead of wrapping.
8. **Tabs are framed.** `FormTabs` renders `TabsList variant="line"` inside a
   `rounded-sm border-2 border-border p-2` frame, matching group/array.
9. **Item controls live on the item header.** `AccordionTrigger` takes `actions`, rendered
   after the trigger and before `AccordionTriggerChevron` (a sibling chevron that reads the
   trigger's `aria-expanded` via `peer/accordion-trigger` and forwards clicks). `FormArray`
   hands a group-shaped item's actions to its `FormGroup` through `ArrayItemActionsContext`
   (reset to `null` inside the group); scalar items keep them beside the input.
   `BlockAccordionItem` places `BlockActionsMenu` before the same chevron.
10. **No remount on drop.** `DndProvider` no longer re-keys `DragDropContext` after a drag
    and no longer keeps per-droppable slot UUIDs. `useAccordionDndState({ storeKey,
    defaultOpen })` uses a `useId` item value, and `FormGroup` keys stored open state by the
    innermost array item's stored `id` plus its path below it — so arrow moves, drags and
    preview-toggle remounts all keep each item's open state, and a drop never collapses and
    regrows the form under the scroller.
11. **Duplicate copies live values.** `FormArray`'s duplicate reads `field.getValue()` at click
    time, not the render-time `field.state.value` snapshot.
12. **Array item header and controls.** `ArrayItemHeaderContext` (replacing the
    actions-only context) carries a group item's drag handle — rendered through
    `AccordionTrigger`'s new `leading` slot, left of the label — its actions, and the array's
    Collapse all / Expand all signal (`{ version, open }`; `FormGroup` applies only versions
    newer than its mount). `FormArray` shows an `N/max <plural>` count with Collapse all /
    Expand all for group items, moves the add button below the items, and its empty state
    reads `No <labels.plural> yet.`; `apps/test`'s `fields` arrays now set `labels`.
13. **Edits inside array/blocks items save.** `isFieldKeyDirty` matched nested meta only by
    `<key>.`; an item edit registers as `<key>[n].field`, so `changedValues` returned `{}` and
    `onSubmit` returned before the mutation — a silent no-op save. It now also matches
    `<key>[`.
14. **Header rows.** Array items pass `index`, so a group item reads `[n] - <label>`.
    `FormArray`'s label and `N/max <plural>` count share one centered row with Collapse all /
    Expand all; `FormBlocks` takes the field `label` and renders it with its count on the same
    row as its header actions.
15. **`sideEffects` lists `./src/adapter.ts`.** `testing/*`' bare `import "../adapter"` fixes
    evaluation order across the registry → adapter → components cycle (vitest needs it);
    esbuild dropped it with `ignored-bare-import` because the package declared the source
    pure. Consumers load `dist/*`, so their tree-shaking is unaffected.
16. **Hidden containers mount only while they hold an error.** Base UI unmounts inactive
    `Tabs.Panel`s and closed `Accordion.Panel`s, so a field in an inactive tab or collapsed
    container was unregistered when submit validation ran: its error stayed on the form-level
    `errorMap` only, the badge counted 0, and the input showed no message after switching.
    `collectErroredPaths` reads both `fieldMeta` errors and the form-level per-path maps;
    `FormTabs` (per panel), `FormCollapsible`, `FormGroup` and `BlockAccordionItem` pass
    `keepMounted={errorCount > 0}`, so error-free hidden content still unmounts.
17. **Named-tab badge.** `FormTabsTrigger` counts a named tab's errors under its own
    `name` (`seo`), since its fields store at `seo.*`, not at their own keys.
18. **Polish.** Array and tabs frames use `px-3 py-2` like every collapsible; a single
    relationship's picker button reads `Select <label>`; block item actions order copy,
    duplicate, move up/down, insert above/below, paste above/below, remove (Copy uses
    `ClipboardCopyIcon`, distinct from Duplicate's `CopyIcon`).
19. **Scroll to the first error.** TanStack Form has no focus-on-error option. On a failed
    submit (`failedSubmitAttemptOf`), `FormTabs` selects its first errored tab (unless the
    active one has an error) and every collapsed container holding an error opens; `AppForm`
    re-runs `form.validate("submit")` so the newly mounted fields receive their errors, waits
    `ACCORDION_TRANSITION_MS`, then scrolls the innermost visible `[data-field-invalid]`
    wrapper (set by `FieldSlotOutlet`) to the center of its nearest overflowing scroller and
    focuses its control — not `scrollIntoView`, which also scrolled the shell's `main` past
    its bottom. This replaced the views' `findErroredTopLevelTab` + `?<fieldKey>=` jump,
    which is removed. Both edit-view form scrollers are `relative`: absolutely positioned
    descendants (`sr-only` labels, hidden checkbox inputs, icons) otherwise took the
    `relative` `<form>` outside the scroller as their containing block, escaped its clipping,
    and stretched the shell's `main` to ~3.5k px — a second, outer scrollbar.
20. **Plain array rows.** A non-group item renders its input with `HideFieldLabelContext`
    (its `FormLabel` becomes `sr-only`), the item number sits in the gutter beside the drag
    handle, and the gutter and controls are `h-8` — the input's height — so they line up
    with the input.
21. **Block header actions.** `blocks.item.actions` contributions receive `placement`
    (`"inline" | "menu"`); duplicate, move up/down and remove render as header icon buttons
    from `sm` up (menu items below), with the same icons as the array item controls; copy,
    insert and paste stay in the ⋯ menu. The inline pass receives only project hide
    directives, so `{ id, hidden: true }` hides a built-in on both surfaces and project-added
    actions stay in the menu.
22. **`array()` has no `labels`.** The array's own `label` is the plural and `items.label`
    the singular, read through core's `arrayPluralLabel` / `arrayItemLabel` (falling back to
    `DEFAULT_ARRAY_LABEL` "Items" / `DEFAULT_ARRAY_ITEM_LABEL` "Item"); `FormArray` and
    `ArrayFieldCell` use them. `apps/docs` `fields/array.mdx` still documents `labels` —
    updated in the commit phase.
23. **Field header actions: inline or ⋯, never both.** A blocks field's header actions (Copy all,
    Paste, Replace all, Collapse all, Expand all) render as text buttons on the label row while
    the header row is at least `BLOCKS_HEADER_INLINE_MIN_PX` (640) wide — measured on the row
    itself by `useMeasuredCompact(ref, px)` — and inside one `ActionsMenu` ⋯ otherwise; an
    array's Collapse all / Expand all follow `useCompactForm()` the same way. Both use the shared
    `HeaderAction`; `blocks.header.actions` contributions receive `placement` and
    `onReplaceAllRequest`, and the Replace all confirmation dialog lives in `FormBlocks`.
24. **Layout follows the form column, not the viewport.** Both edit-view scrollers are named
    `form` containers (`[container-name:form]`) and `AppForm`'s `<form>` is `@container/form`
    (nearest wins). Thresholds: sidebar beside the fields from `@3xl` (48rem), stacked below
    otherwise; `FieldLayoutItem`/row widths from `@xl` (36rem). Item actions are either/or,
    decided by a measured `useCompactForm()` (`FormCompactContext`, `ResizeObserver` at
    `FORM_COMPACT_WIDTH_PX` = 512, provided by `AppForm` and by `FormCompactProvider` around the
    edit views' form column) because menu content portals outside any container query: array
    items show inline `SurfacedAction` icons when wide and only a ⋯ menu when compact; blocks
    show duplicate/move/remove icons plus a ⋯ with copy/insert/paste when wide (the surfaced
    built-ins get hide directives in the menu outlet), and one ⋯ with every action when compact.
    Group headers truncate and
    hide the field count, block headers hide the type badge, the upload empty state stacks and
    upload rows truncate, all below `@lg`; the tab strip scrolls horizontally. The live-preview
    panel is a `preview` container: device buttons from `@2xl`, a single width dropdown below.
25. **`condition` on the base admin types; `mask` on the per-type ones; field utils in one
    file.** `FieldAdminConfigInput`/`FieldAdminConfig` (now `<TCollectionSlug, TComponent>`)
    and `UIFieldAdminInput`/`UIFieldAdminConfig` (now `<TCollectionSlug>`) declare `condition`;
    the base field types pass their slug into `admin` (Design Decision 33). The admin types
    that only added `condition` are deleted — array, checkbox, color, date, json, richtext,
    textarea, upload, row, tabs — and those fields inherit `admin`. text/email/number/url's
    `mask` moved from an `& { mask }` intersection on `admin` into their own
    `<Type>FieldAdminInput`/`<Type>FieldAdminConfig`. Every function from `fields/ui/utils.ts`
    (`andFieldConditions`, `isFieldConditionMet`, `hasFieldConditions`, `resolveRowWidths`,
    `getDataFields`, `getUIFieldsWithCell`) moved into `fields/utils.ts` under a "Field
    traversal, conditions and row layout" heading, with its tests in `fields/utils.test.ts`;
    the public exports are unchanged. The generated API reference in `apps/docs`
    (`api/core/src/interfaces/*`) still lists the deleted types — regenerated in the commit phase.
26. **Menu order, row icons, counters.** Compact blocks header ⋯: Collapse all, Expand all,
    separator, then Copy all / Paste / Replace all (inline keeps the contributed actions first).
    Block item built-ins are ordered duplicate, move up/down, insert above/below, copy, paste
    above/below, remove. Relationship and upload rows render the drag handle only when
    reorderable (no reserved blank slot); a relationship row shows the target collection's
    `admin.icon` (12px, `translate-y-px` to sit on the title's visual centre) before the title.
    Their remove (X) button is `p-0`, so the row's own `px-2` sets both edges symmetrically.
    `textarea` always shows a character count — `n/max` with `max`, bare `n` without.
    `FormDescription` carries `data-slot="form-description"`, which the input contract now
    asserts on (a bare `p.text-muted-foreground` also matched the counter). The contract's
    round-trip check waits for the control value (CodeMirror applies typed input
    asynchronously, so the json case failed under full-suite load).

## Verification

Run after every step and once at the end:

```bash
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm --filter test typecheck
pnpm --filter www typecheck
```

Then the Step 18 browser smoke checklist against the developer's running `apps/test` admin
(P-024 — attach, never start a dev server). The spec is done when all four commands are green
and every checklist item is recorded as passing.
